newsitem.title: JAPAN: France's Arthuis says Euro is stabilising factor.
newsitem.headline: France's Arthuis says Euro is stabilising factor.

text.p: The advent of the Euro, or the European single currency, is an undeniable stabilising force for currency markets, French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Sunday.

"The players of the economic game suffer when currencies fluctuate because it make them reassess their costs and billings," Arthuis told Reuters at a reception for French residents in Japan. "The (advent of the) Euro is undeniably a stabilising factor," he added.
"In Europe, we also need stability," he said. "A good parity is one which allows us to obtain durable and low interest rates," he said.
Asked whether he included France in the equation, he repeated that a good parity is one which allows for the lowest possible interest rates.

Asked whether the yen's current rate reflects the economy's fundamentals Arthuis said: "It's the markets which fix parity while taking into consideration the economic conditions of each country, its competitiveness, and interest rates."
"Its not surprising the Japanese monetary authorities have chosen such modest interest rates," he added. "It has changed a lot the currency's parity since 1995," he said.
